newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks race to record high at close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks race to record high at close.

text.p: Mexico's stock market raced to a record closing high on Tuesday as investors welcomed an ambitious economic plan to spur growth and keep a lid on inflation, dealers said.
The IPC index of 37 leading shares closed up 57.24 points, or 1.43 percent, to 4,060.06 points. Volume was firm at 132 million shares.
"The market looked good. The government economic plan helped. It offered continuity in economic policy for the next few years," said Diego Candano, head of analysis at Ixe Brokerage firm.
President Ernesto Zedillo unveiled the National Program to Finance Development, a plan calling for five percent economic growth a year and inflation of 7.5 percent by 2000.
The plan also called for allowing a current account deficit to grow to 3.2 percent of GDP by 2000.
Analysts said the plan was welcome, but probably too optimistic, especially 5.6 percent GDP growth for 2000, an election year.
Stocks hit an intraday high of 4,071.86 points, but dealers said sell orders tamed the gains.
"There was normal profit-taking, especially since interest rates are seeing going up (later in the day)," Candano said.
A Reuters survey of money market dealers forecast a rise in the 28-day Cetes, or T-bills, or 71 basis points to about 19.02 percent.
